description: An interactive, non-legal assessment that helps emerging companies sanity-check document readiness before fundraising.

defaultPrompt: Help me assess my company’s financing readiness.
Help me compare my company records against a financing-readiness checklist.
Build a data-room index and prioritized preparation plan.
interface.longDescription:
Prepare for financing with a clearer picture of your company's records and a practical plan for what to organize next.

ECVC Financing Readiness helps founders and emerging-company teams turn scattered information into a structured preparation checklist. See which records appear accounted for, which need attention, and which questions remain unanswered before initial investor diligence.

Start with guided questions, review of documents you choose to provide, or both. An optional pitch deck can help prefill company context; its claims are flagged for confirmation, not treated as proof.

The seven-step assessment covers company and governance records; capitalization; people, intellectual property and digital assets; financial and tax organization; commercial agreements, privacy and regulatory records; disputes and investigations; and data-room organization.

Get a provisional process-readiness score alongside assessment completeness and reviewed-evidence coverage, so the result shows both your preparation and the limits of the information available. A category summary and prioritized action plan help your team decide what to organize first.

When requested, create an editable readiness report, workbook, or data-room index and action plan in a format supported by your environment. A data-room index is an organizational aid, not a hosted data room.

Provided by Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman LLP. Workflow author: Steve Ryan.

This plugin provides general information and organizational guidance, not legal or investment advice. It does not determine legal validity, ownership, enforceability, compliance or investment suitability, or predict whether financing will succeed. Use does not create an attorney-client relationship. Share only materials you are authorized to provide and remove unnecessary sensitive information.
